items.stem: In alphabetical filing, which name is filed FIRST?  Carlos A. Pedro | Dr. Teresita B. Juan | Engr. Imelda E. Del Rosario | Ernesto F. Flores

reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Engr. Imelda E. Del Rosario → DELROSARIO, Imelda; Ernesto F. Flores → FLORES, Ernesto; Dr. Teresita B. Juan → JUAN, Teresita; Carlos A. Pedro → PEDRO, Carlos.
reveal.why_correct: "Engr. Imelda E. Del Rosario" is right. It comes first when every name is indexed surname first, letter by letter. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o1: "Carlos A. Pedro" sorts by the given name. Personal names file by surname first.
why_wrong.o2: "Ernesto F. Flores" files the prefix as a separate word (for example "Dela Cruz" under C). A prefix joins the rest of the surname.
why_wrong.o4: "Dr. Teresita B. Juan" sorts by the title (Dr., Atty., Engr.). A title is only the last unit.
